PHYSICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Projectile Motion ● Free fall. ● Projectile motion ● . ● Trajectory motion. ● Ac? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Projectile Motion ● Free fall. ● Projectile motion ● . ● Trajectory motion. ● Ac.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Projectile Motion ● Free fall. ● Projectile motion ● . ● Trajectory motion. ● Ac.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Projectile Motion ● Free fall. ● Projectile motion ● . ● Trajectory motion. ● Ac.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Projectile Motion ● Free fall. ● Projectile motion ● . ● Trajectory motion. ● Ac.

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

5. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Nitrogen gas only

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fluid Flow ● Types of fluid flow (steady flow, unsteady flow, laminar flow, turb? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fluid Flow ● Types of fluid flow (steady flow, unsteady flow, laminar flow, turb.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Fluid Flow ● Types of fluid flow (steady flow, unsteady flow, laminar flow, turb.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fluid Flow ● Types of fluid flow (steady flow, unsteady flow, laminar flow, turb.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fluid Flow ● Types of fluid flow (steady flow, unsteady flow, laminar flow, turb.

8. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

9. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

10. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Capacitors 3.2 Magnetic effect of electric current 3.3 Diodes 4.0 Environmental ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Capacitors 3.2 Magnetic effect of electric current 3.3 Diodes 4.0 Environmental .
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Capacitors 3.2 Magnetic effect of electric current 3.3 Diodes 4.0 Environmental .
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Capacitors 3.2 Magnetic effect of electric current 3.3 Diodes 4.0 Environmental .
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Capacitors 3.2 Magnetic effect of electric current 3.3 Diodes 4.0 Environmental .

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thermionic emission and its applications ● Production of cathode rays and their ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thermionic emission and its applications ● Production of cathode rays and their .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Thermionic emission and its applications ● Production of cathode rays and their .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Thermionic emission and its applications ● Production of cathode rays and their .
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thermionic emission and its applications ● Production of cathode rays and their .

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Physics of Wind Formation ● Wind patterns (polar easterlies, westerlies, horse l and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Rockets Page 12 of 47 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYSICS and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Rocket Science ● Rocket ● Main parts of a rocket. ● The forces i and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Fluid Flow ● Types of fluid flow (steady flow, unsteady flow, laminar flow, turb and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
